findings.title: remove() now always queries the database for the IDP
findings.body: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is now executed unconditionally at the top of `remove()`. Before this change, the DB lookup only happened when the alias cache key was invalidated; the common path used the cached entry. Every removal now incurs an extra uncached DB read, even when the cache already holds the IDP. The lookup should be deferred to the branch that needs it, or the cached model should be reused for the login invalidation check.

findings.title: Cleanup removes a non-existent IDP named "alias" instead of the created alias
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` uses the literal string "alias" rather than the alias of the IDP just created. The same mistake appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. The created IDPs are therefore never cleaned up, and they leak into other tests in the class and the shared realm. The cleanup should reference the actual alias (for example via a lambda that captures the alias variable). The same pre-existing pattern in `testCacheIDPByOrg` is copied here.

findings.title: getForLogin javadoc omits the new organization public-broker requirement
findings.body: The javadoc says an IDP is usable for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. The `getLoginPredicate()` change at line 254 adds a further requirement: an IDP linked to an organization must also have `BROKER_PUBLIC` set to true. The documented contract no longer matches the behaviour, so callers relying on the Javadoc will get wrong expectations about which IDPs are returned.
